assistant_turns.name: turn-0003-dismiss-basis

assistant_turns.assistant_reply: Under Travis County Appeal Board decision AB-2025-114, if the agency cannot produce radar/lidar calibration records on timely request, the speed measurement is unreliable and the citation must be dismissed. The hearing notes confirm calibration records were not produced, so dismissal is supported.

assistant_turns.name: turn-0004-penalty

business_rules.name: r1
business_rules.title: Citation requires driver, violation and jurisdiction
business_rules.description: A citation must reference exactly one driver, one violation type, and one issuing jurisdiction.

business_rules.name: r2
business_rules.title: Response due date is derived from the jurisdiction
business_rules.description: ResponseDueDate = IssuedOn + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond. Changing the jurisdiction's rule re-derives every citation under it.

business_rules.name: r3
business_rules.title: A response is pay or contest
business_rules.description: Responding means either paying the fine or requesting a hearing; either sets RespondedOn and advances the citation to Responded.

business_rules.name: r10
business_rules.title: Citation status is computed, never stored
business_rules.description: CitationStatus is re-derived on every read from raw facts and child events; there is no stored status column to drift.

business_rules.name: r11
business_rules.title: No response by deadline is a default judgment
business_rules.description: If the response window passes with no RespondedOn, the citation moves to Adjudicated by default.

business_rules.name: r12
business_rules.title: Contest status follows the latest hearing
business_rules.description: ContestStatus is derived from the newest related hearing: NotContested | HearingRequested → Scheduled → Heard.

business_rules.name: r13
business_rules.title: Only a manager schedules a hearing
business_rules.description: Transitioning a hearing from HearingRequested to Scheduled is a manager-role action.

business_rules.name: r20
business_rules.title: Fine is the violation's base fine
business_rules.description: The amount owed starts at the violation type's BaseFineUsd for the citation's jurisdiction.

business_rules.name: r21
business_rules.title: Late payment incurs a jurisdiction penalty
business_rules.description: If payment is not made by the pay-by date, a penalty of LatePenaltyPct of the fine is added.

business_rules.name: r22
business_rules.title: Prolonged non-payment goes to collections
business_rules.description: A Late citation becomes Collections after DaysLateToCollections days past the pay-by date.

business_rules.name: r23
business_rules.title: A dismissed citation owes nothing
business_rules.description: If a hearing dismisses the citation, PaymentStatus is NotOwed regardless of the fine.

business_rules.name: r30
business_rules.title: Active points roll up to the driver
business_rules.description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from adjudicated, non-dismissed citations.

business_rules.name: r31
business_rules.title: Points drive license warning then suspension
business_rules.description: LicenseStatus is Warning at the jurisdiction's PointWarningThreshold and Suspended at PointSuspensionThreshold.

business_rules.name: r40
business_rules.title: Regulations are data, not code
business_rules.description: Every regulatory knob — deadlines, fines, penalties, thresholds, school caps — is a column on Jurisdictions, editable without code changes.

business_rules.name: r50
business_rules.title: Overdue work is urgent
business_rules.description: A work-queue item whose due date is in the past is urgent and sorts to the top.

business_rules.name: r51
business_rules.title: Work items mirror their subject's deadline
business_rules.description: A work item's DueDate is carried from its subject (e.g. Citations.ResponseDueDate or PaymentDueDate).

business_rules.name: r60
business_rules.title: Overrides require a reason
business_rules.description: Any OVERRIDE audit entry must carry a non-empty Reason; the trail is append-only.

business_rules.name: r70
business_rules.title: Every assistant turn is costed
business_rules.description: Each assistant turn records input/output tokens and the exact pricing version used, so TotalCost is fully derivable.

business_rules.name: tt-intake-01
business_rules.title: Citation requires driver, violation, jurisdiction
business_rules.description: A citation must reference exactly one Driver, one ViolationType, and one issuing Jurisdiction; none may be null at intake.

business_rules.name: tt-intake-02
business_rules.title: Issue date present and not future-dated
business_rules.description: Every citation records an IssueDate that is on or before today; a future issue date is rejected at intake.

business_rules.name: tt-intake-03
business_rules.title: Driver response is pay-or-contest before the deadline
business_rules.description: The driver's response is one of {pay, contest} and must be recorded on or before the computed ResponseDeadline.

business_rules.name: tt-deadline-01
business_rules.title: Response deadline derives from jurisdiction DaysToRespond
business_rules.description: ResponseDeadline = IssueDate + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond; it recomputes whenever the rule changes.

business_rules.name: tt-citation-01
business_rules.title: Citation status is derived, never stored
business_rules.description: CitationStatus (Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed) is computed on read from facts and child CaseEvents; no stored status column is authoritative.

business_rules.name: tt-citation-02
business_rules.title: Status order is monotonic
business_rules.description: A citation may only advance forward through its lifecycle states; backward transitions require an explicit, logged override.

business_rules.name: tt-contest-01
business_rules.title: Contesting requires a timely contest response
business_rules.description: The contest track only opens when DriverResponse = contest was recorded before the ResponseDeadline.

business_rules.name: tt-contest-02
business_rules.title: Contest track derives from the latest hearing
business_rules.description: ContestStatus (NotContested | HearingRequested -> Scheduled -> Heard) is derived from the most recent Hearings row for the citation.

business_rules.name: tt-contest-03
business_rules.title: Determination decides liability
business_rules.description: A hearing outcome of dismissed sets liability to none and zero fine owed; upheld confirms the original fine and points.

business_rules.name: tt-hearing-01
business_rules.title: Hearing requires a requested contest
business_rules.description: A Hearings row may only be created for a citation whose ContestStatus is HearingRequested or later.

business_rules.name: tt-hearing-02
business_rules.title: Scheduling is manager-or-admin only
business_rules.description: Only manager or admin roles may set a hearing's ScheduledDate; representatives request, they do not schedule.

business_rules.name: tt-payment-01
business_rules.title: Payment track derives from payments and pay-by date
business_rules.description: PaymentStatus (Pending -> Due -> Late -> Collections | Paid | NotOwed) is computed from Payments rows and the jurisdiction pay-by date.

business_rules.name: tt-payment-02
business_rules.title: Late penalty applies after the pay-by date
business_rules.description: Once the pay-by date passes with no full payment, the jurisdiction's LatePenaltyPercent is added to AmountOwed.

business_rules.name: tt-payment-03
business_rules.title: Paid in full closes the case
business_rules.description: When recorded Payments equal AmountOwed, PaymentStatus becomes Paid and the citation advances toward Closed.

business_rules.name: tt-fee-01
business_rules.title: Base fine comes from the violation and jurisdiction
business_rules.description: The base fine is the ViolationType base amount adjusted by the jurisdiction's fee schedule; it is data, not a constant.

business_rules.name: tt-license-01
business_rules.title: Active points roll up across a driver's citations
business_rules.description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from non-dismissed, non-expired citations under each jurisdiction's point window.

business_rules.name: tt-license-02
business_rules.title: License track follows jurisdiction thresholds
business_rules.description: LicenseStatus (Valid -> Warning -> Suspended) is derived by comparing ActivePoints against the jurisdiction's warning and suspension thresholds.

business_rules.name: tt-queue-01
business_rules.title: Work queue is computed from deadlines and status
business_rules.description: WorkQueueItems are derived from overdue responses, due/late payments, and upcoming hearings, bucketed by urgency; nothing is hand-enqueued.

business_rules.name: tt-audit-01
business_rules.title: Every state-affecting change is logged
business_rules.description: Each status change, override, payment, and edit writes an append-only AuditLogEntries (and where lifecycle-relevant, a CaseEvents) row.

business_rules.name: tt-audit-02
business_rules.title: The log never contradicts the derived state
business_rules.description: The append-only history explains how current computed state was reached; it is additive narration, never an alternate source of truth.

business_rules.name: tt-assistant-01
business_rules.title: Assistant answers are grounded in live data
business_rules.description: The assistant answers about a citation/rule/portal from live vw_* reads and the rulebook, recording each exchange as an AssistantTurns row.

business_rules.name: tt-assistant-02
business_rules.title: Every turn is cost-accounted
business_rules.description: Each AssistantTurns row records input/output tokens and a computed cost via ModelPricingVersions for the turn's AiModel.

business_rules.name: tt-rules-01
business_rules.title: Jurisdiction knobs are editable data
business_rules.description: Deadlines, fines, penalty percentages, and point thresholds live in Jurisdictions/JurisdictionRules and every dependent value re-derives on edit.

business_rules.name: tt-rules-02
business_rules.title: Each jurisdiction rule cites its source
business_rules.description: A JurisdictionRules row links to the JurisdictionSourceDocuments / ReferenceDocuments authority that justifies it.

business_rules.name: tt-rbac-01
business_rules.title: Four canonical roles govern access
business_rules.description: Exactly four roles exist (admin, manager, representative, external-llm) and every permission decision references one of them.

business_rules.name: tt-rbac-02
business_rules.title: CRUD is per role, per table, per field
business_rules.description: What each role may create/read/update/delete is data at the table and field grain; the enforced API consults it on every operation.

business_rules.name: tt-rbac-03
business_rules.title: Row access follows per-role WHERE policies
business_rules.description: Each role-table pair carries a WHERE policy; a representative sees only their own citations while admin sees all, enforced on every vw_* read.

business_rules.name: tt-rbac-04
business_rules.title: Lower-trust roles get redacted projections
business_rules.description: Fields denied to a role (e.g. PII for external-llm) are stripped from responses at projection time, not nulled afterward.

business_rules.name: tt-nav-01
business_rules.title: Navigation is derived from PlatformNaviation rows
business_rules.description: The sidebar and route tree render from PlatformNaviation filtered by the current role's RoleVisibility; there is no hand-maintained menu.

business_rules.name: tt-nav-02
business_rules.title: Route order and pinning are data
business_rules.description: NavLevel, SortOrder, and PinToTop on PlatformNaviation determine ordering and which screens float to the top.

business_rules.name: tt-auth-01
business_rules.title: Identity is resolved per request from the magic-link session
business_rules.description: Each request resolves to an AppUsers row and role via the MagicLinkConfig flow; identity feeds every RBAC and scoping decision.

business_rules.name: tt-license-pkg-01
business_rules.title: Surfaces are gated by license/active flags
business_rules.description: Packages, features, tables, and routes carry IsLicensed/IsActive flags; unlicensed surfaces are revealed as upgrade prompts, not deleted.

business_rules.name: tt-platform-01
business_rules.title: The rulebook JSON is the single source of truth
business_rules.description: All substrates (Postgres, Python, explain-dag, rulespeak) are mechanically derived from the rulebook by effortless build; edits go to the rulebook.

business_rules.name: tt-platform-02
business_rules.title: The platform describes itself
business_rules.description: ERBTables/ERBFields/ERBFeatures/ERBPackages catalog every table, field, capability, and package so the app can render its own model.

business_rules.name: tt-platform-03
business_rules.title: Build is generate + load; drift is guarded
business_rules.description: effortless build regenerates DDL/views/inserts and reloads the DB; a drift guard warns before a rebuild would clobber un-saved DB edits.

business_rules.name: tt-glossary-01
business_rules.title: Domain terms are defined as data
business_rules.description: Every domain term used in a feature or rule is defined in GlossaryTerms under a GlossaryCategories group.

business_rules.name: tt-determination-01
business_rules.title: Determination is recorded
business_rules.description: A hearing determination (upheld / dismissed / reduced) must be recorded on the Citation before the citation-lifecycle may advance to adjudicated, and it writes a CaseEvents entry.

business_rules.name: tt-determination-02
business_rules.title: Dismissal reverses consequences
business_rules.description: When a determination dismisses a Citation, any assessed license points are reversed and any paid amount is refunded, restoring the Driver to make-whole state.

business_rules.name: tt-state-01
business_rules.title: Lifecycle transitions are guarded
business_rules.description: Every state transition is gated by its guard condition and the firing role; the state-machine backbone rejects illegal transitions and logs each accepted one to CaseEvents.

erb_features.name: citation-intake
erb_features.title: Citation Intake
erb_features.description: Record a new traffic citation — driver, violation type, issuing jurisdiction, issue date — and immediately derive its response deadline from the jurisdiction's DaysToRespond rule.
erb_features.source_text: Records a new traffic citation as a row in the Citations table -- driver (FK to Drivers), violation type (FK to ViolationTypes), issuing jurisdiction (FK to Jurisdictions), and issue date -- and immediately derives the response deadline from the jurisdiction's DaysToRespond rule via vw_citations. An admin or representative captures the citation off a paper ticket and the computed ResponseDeadline column appears the moment the row is saved, with no manual date math. This is the front door of the whole citation-lifecycle state machine.

erb_features.name: driver-response

erb_features.source_text: Captures the driver's choice -- pay now or request a hearing -- writing it onto the Citations row and advancing the citation from Issued to Responded in vw_citations before the response window closes. A representative records the decision on behalf of the cited driver, and the contest-track state machine branches on it. The response and its timestamp become CaseEvents rows so the audit trail explains every move.

erb_features.name: citation-statemachine

erb_features.description: Show the live Citation status (Issued → Responded → InContest → Adjudicated → Closed) re-derived from facts and child events — never a stored, drifting column.
erb_features.source_text: Shows the live Citation status (Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed) re-derived on every read from facts and child CaseEvents rows in vw_citations -- never a stored, drifting column. erb_features.name: payment-track

erb_features.description: Compute the payment track (Pending → Due → Late → Collections | Paid | NotOwed) including the jurisdiction-specific late penalty once the pay-by date passes.
erb_features.source_text: Computes the payment track (Pending -> Due -> Late -> Collections | Paid | NotOwed) on vw_citations, including the jurisdiction-specific late penalty once the pay-by date passes, by joining Citations, Payments, and the jurisdiction's penalty rule. A representative or driver sees the live amount owed and its escalation status. The Late and Collections transitions are the ones the deadline-driven work queue watches most.

erb_features.name: core-role-permission-model
erb_features.title: Role→Table→Field CRUD permission model
erb_features.description: Additive/subtractive CRUD permissions. Resolution per (role,table,field,op): effective = ERBFields.{Role}CRUD ?? ERBTables.{Role}CRUD ?? Roles.DefaultCRUD (field overrides table overrides role default; NULL inherits the parent). op_allowed = effective CONTAINS the C/R/U/D letter (no dashes; e.g. CRUD, RU, RD). Derived {Role}Can{Op} booleans are BLANK when the source is NULL so inherit is distinguishable from explicit deny. Seed posture: Admin/Manager DefaultCRUD=CRUD, Rep/External-LLM=R; table grants NULL; calculated/lookup/aggregation fields pinned to R, raw fields NULL.
erb_features.status_description: Modeled in the rulebook; not yet part of the official build everyone sees.
erb_features.source_text: Encodes the Role -> Table -> Field CRUD permission model as data so that what each role may create, read, update, or delete is a row, not a hardcoded guard. An admin edits a grid and the enforced CRUD API changes behavior immediately. This declarative matrix is the backbone of the platform's RBAC.

erb_features.name: core-table-where-policies
erb_features.title: Per-role table WHERE policies
erb_features.description: Each ERBTables row carries a {Role}WHERE clause that limits vertical (row) access per role — the source for the derived RLS plan.
erb_features.status_description: Modeled in the rulebook; not yet part of the official build everyone sees.
erb_features.source_text: Stores a per-role row-scoping WHERE policy per table so a representative sees only their own citations while an admin sees all, expressed as data the enforced API compiles into vw_* reads. An admin authors the policy once and every query for that role is filtered. Row-level security becomes configuration, not code.

erb_features.title: App-Users directory & user management
erb_features.description: A searchable directory of every AppUser, groupable by role, with create-user and a per-user detail page (profile + inherited-access view). This is the people side of access control, paired with the Roles catalog.
erb_features.source_text: Provides the App-Users directory backed by the AppUsers table for creating, editing, and assigning roles to users. An admin manages who can log in and what role they hold. Every identity the magic-link flow resolves lives here.

erb_features.name: core-admin-equivalent-access
erb_features.title: Admin-equivalent cross-world access
erb_features.description: Roles flagged admin-equivalent may browse any role's URL world (/admin, /reps, /llm); everyone else is bounced to their own home world. This is what lets an administrator move freely across the three role surfaces.
erb_features.source_text: Grants admin (and admin-equivalent) roles cross-world access so they can read and act across every jurisdiction and every representative's caseload, enforced via the WHERE policies. An admin troubleshoots any citation regardless of owner. The breadth is itself a configured policy, not a hardcoded superuser bypass.

erb_features.name: core-role-url-worlds
erb_features.title: Role URL worlds (/admin · /reps · /llm)
erb_features.description: Every role gets its own slug-prefixed URL world, so the same React app presents a different navigable surface per role. The home world, redirects, and sidebar all key off the active slug.
erb_features.source_text: Routes each role into its own URL world (/admin, /reps, /llm) so navigation, scoping, and chrome match the actor, driven by PlatformNaviation RoleVisibility. A representative lands in /reps and sees only their tools. The same rulebook produces a tailored app per role.

erb_features.name: core-role-impersonation
erb_features.title: Role impersonation (view-as-role)
erb_features.description: An admin can browse the platform exactly as another (redacted) role sees it by entering the External-LLM world, which sends an X-Impersonate-Role header so the API returns that role's filtered, redacted projection.
erb_features.source_text: Lets an admin view-as-role to see precisely what a representative or external-llm would see, applying that role's permission and WHERE policies live. An admin verifies redaction and scoping by walking in the role's shoes. It is a debugging superpower that never weakens the real policies.

erb_features.name: core-default-crud-editor
erb_features.title: Per-role default CRUD editor
erb_features.description: The four-state Create/Read/Update/Delete control at the top of the cascade: each role's default posture is set with an inherit / grant / deny tri-state, and every table and field falls back to it unless overridden.
erb_features.source_text: Provides a per-role default CRUD editor that sets the baseline create/read/update/delete a role gets on a table before field-level overrides, stored as permission rows. An admin sets sane defaults once. Field grids then refine the exceptions.

erb_features.name: core-table-where-policy-editor
erb_features.title: Per-table CRUD + WHERE policy editor
erb_features.description: On each table's detail page an admin sets per-role CRUD overrides and a per-role WHERE clause that limits which rows that role can see. The WHERE policies are the source for the derived row-level-security plan.
erb_features.source_text: A per-table CRUD + WHERE policy editor where an admin authors the row-scoping expression that filters a role's reads of that table's vw_*. An admin writes 'driver = current_user' once for representatives. The enforced API compiles it on every query.

erb_features.name: core-field-crud-grid
erb_features.title: Per-field CRUD permission grid
erb_features.description: A column-level grid where each field's CRUD is granted or denied per role. Denied fields drop out of that role's column-limited views, which is how role-specific schemas are produced.
erb_features.source_text: A per-field CRUD permission grid that controls, column by column, what each role may read or write across every table, persisted as permission rows that the role-specific schemas derive from. An admin redacts a PII column for external-llm with one toggle. Granularity is data, not branching code.

erb_features.name: core-redaction-sweep
erb_features.title: Role-wide PII redaction sweep
erb_features.description: Marking a role redacted runs a one-click sweep that bulk-denies every PII field carrying a *Redacted sibling, so the role transparently receives masked values instead of raw personal data across all tables.
erb_features.source_text: Runs a role-wide PII redaction sweep that flags every sensitive field (driver address, license number) and ensures the field grid denies it to lower-trust roles. An admin confirms no PII leaks to external-llm in one pass. The sweep reads the field catalog and the grid together.

erb_features.name: core-redacted-projection
erb_features.title: Redacted-response projection
erb_features.description: When a redacted role (or an impersonation/LLM session) reads data, the server swaps in *_redacted columns so personal identifiers are masked in the response body itself — not merely hidden in the UI.
erb_features.source_text: Produces the redacted-response projection the enforced API returns to a role, stripping denied columns from every vw_* result before it leaves the server. An external-llm receives a citation with PII columns absent, not nulled-after-the-fact. Redaction happens at projection time, deterministically.

erb_features.name: core-derived-rls
erb_features.title: Derived row-level security enforcement
erb_features.description: The per-role WHERE policies and CRUD grants are compiled into role-scoped Postgres views and a search_path so that reads are filtered in the database itself, regardless of what the API or UI does.
erb_features.source_text: Enforces derived row-level security by applying the compiled WHERE-policy plan to every read, so a representative's query of vw_citations is silently scoped to their own rows. A rep simply cannot fetch another rep's data. The enforcement is generated from the rulebook, audited, and uniform.

erb_features.name: core-live-identity
erb_features.title: Live per-request identity resolution
erb_features.description: The JWT carries only an email; the role, redaction flag, and licensing visibility are looked up live from AppUsers on every request, so revoking or re-roling a user takes effect immediately without re-issuing tokens.
erb_features.source_text: Resolves live per-request identity from the magic-link session to an AppUsers row and role on every call, feeding RBAC and scoping with the actual current actor. The platform always knows who is asking right now. Stale or assumed identity is never used.

erb_features.name: core-route-designer
erb_features.title: Route Designer (drag-drop nav tree)
erb_features.description: A live, drag-and-drop editor for the entire platform navigation tree: reparent and reorder routes, edit their fields inline, create and delete routes, and set a per-route CRUD matrix — then SAVE promotes the tree back to the rulebook.
erb_features.source_text: Offers a drag-and-drop Route Designer that edits the PlatformNaviation tree -- parent/child, level, role-visibility, pin-to-top -- as data that the live sidebar renders. An admin reorganizes the whole app's navigation without touching code. The nav tree is rulebook rows end to end.

erb_features.name: core-live-sidebar
erb_features.title: Live DB-driven sidebar
erb_features.description: The sidebar is rendered entirely from the navigation table in the database: package-gated, role-filtered, with empty feature-status buckets auto-hidden and the active record's context grafted in. Edit the routes and the menu changes.
erb_features.source_text: Renders a live DB-driven sidebar straight from PlatformNaviation rows filtered by the current role's RoleVisibility. A user's menu always matches the rulebook and their permissions. There is no hand-maintained menu file to drift.

erb_features.name: core-pin-to-top
erb_features.title: Pin-to-top routes
erb_features.description: A per-route PinToTop flag floats important destinations to the top of the sidebar regardless of their position in the tree, so high-traffic admin pages stay one click away.
erb_features.source_text: Supports pin-to-top routes via a PlatformNaviation.PinToTop flag so high-traffic screens (Work Queue, Citations) float above the long tail. An admin pins the screens reps use most. Ordering is data the sidebar honors.

erb_features.name: core-route-galleries
erb_features.title: By-Role / By-Package route galleries
erb_features.description: Two read-only regroupings of the same navigation set — one grouped by the roles that can reach each route, one by owning package — for auditing coverage at a glance; clicking jumps to that route in the designer tree.
erb_features.source_text: Generates By-Role and By-Package route galleries from PlatformNaviation so an admin can audit the app from either lens -- what each role sees, or what each package contributes. An admin reviews coverage gaps visually. Both galleries are projections of the same nav rows.

erb_features.name: core-route-access-gating
erb_features.title: Per-route access gating
erb_features.description: Visiting a URL a role isn't permitted to read renders an Access-Denied surface instead of the page, enforced in the shell from the same permission data that filters the sidebar — so deep links can't bypass the menu.
erb_features.source_text: Gates each route by RoleVisibility so navigating to a screen a role may not see returns a clean denial instead of a broken page, enforced from PlatformNaviation. A representative who edits the URL still cannot reach an admin screen. Access is checked against the rulebook on every navigation.

erb_features.name: core-nav-backed-pages
erb_features.title: Generic nav-backed pages
erb_features.description: Any navigation row that names a primary_view auto-renders a live, RLS-backed data grid plus a drill-down detail page — no bespoke component required. Most admin catalogs and logs are these generic pages.
erb_features.source_text: Renders generic nav-backed pages: any PlatformNaviation row with a PrimaryTable/PrimaryView gets a working list-or-detail screen with no bespoke component, reading vw_* directly. An admin adds a screen by adding a nav row. The frontend is a renderer of rulebook data.

erb_features.name: core-dev-quick-connect
erb_features.title: Dev quick-connect login
erb_features.description: A development-only login shortcut that lists @example.com demo users and issues a spoofed JWT in one click, so the team can hop between roles locally without the email-code round trip. Gated behind DEV_AUTH_ENABLED.
erb_features.source_text: Provides a dev quick-connect login that authenticates as any seeded AppUsers role for local testing without the full magic-link round trip. A developer hops between admin and representative in one click. It is a convenience that still resolves a real identity and real policies.

erb_features.name: core-unlicensed-reveal
erb_features.title: Unlicensed-surface reveal
erb_features.description: The vendor-only mechanism that lets Effortless staff see surfaces marked unlicensed, while accounts see them hidden. It is the internal key behind every per-feature, per-table, and per-package licensing toggle.
erb_features.source_text: Reveals unlicensed surfaces in a muted state -- features, tables, or routes whose ERBPackage is not licensed are shown as upgrade prompts rather than hidden -- driven by the IsLicensed flags. A buyer sees what the next tier unlocks. Licensing is presentation data, not a deleted feature.

erb_features.name: core-save-to-rulebook
erb_features.title: SAVE: DB → rulebook → rebuild
erb_features.description: The promotion action behind every admin editor: it exports the live admin-config tables out of Postgres back into the rulebook JSON, runs effortless build, then re-initializes the database — turning fast in-DB edits into the new source of truth.
erb_features.source_text: Implements SAVE: edits made in the admin UI write back to the rulebook JSON and trigger a rebuild, so the DB -> rulebook -> rebuild loop closes from inside the app. An admin changes a deadline and the rulebook plus all substrates update. The app edits its own source of truth.

erb_features.name: core-drift-guard
erb_features.title: Rulebook drift guard
erb_features.description: Before a SAVE overwrites the rulebook, a guard checks whether the rulebook is newer than the last build manifest; if so it blocks with a 409 until the operator explicitly forces the write, preventing a stale admin session from clobbering newer changes.
erb_features.source_text: Adds a rulebook drift guard that detects when the live DB diverges from the rulebook JSON and surfaces it before a rebuild silently reverts edits. An admin is warned instead of losing work. The guard protects the SSoT from accidental clobber.

erb_features.name: core-config-export-scope
erb_features.title: Config-export scope
erb_features.description: The defined set of admin-config tables the exporter promotes on SAVE — navigation, packages, roles, tables, fields, endpoints, glossary, business rules, state machines, and branding — deliberately excluding operational data, which resets to seeds on rebuild.
erb_features.source_text: Lets an admin choose the config-export scope -- which packages, tables, and routes ship in an exported rulebook -- so a tenant gets exactly the licensed subset. An admin exports a representative-only build. Scope is selected from the catalog, not edited by hand.

erb_features.name: core-permission-sync
erb_features.title: Non-destructive permission sync
erb_features.description: A script that pushes the rulebook's RBAC matrix into the live database without a full destructive init-db, so permission tweaks can be applied to a running instance while leaving operational data intact.
erb_features.source_text: Performs non-destructive permission sync: when new tables or fields appear, default grants are added without overwriting an admin's existing customizations in the permission grid. An admin upgrades schema and keeps their RBAC edits. Sync is additive by design.

erb_features.name: core-endpoint-access-editor
erb_features.title: Per-endpoint access editor
erb_features.description: An editor for the custom API-endpoint registry where each endpoint, grouped by its subject table, gets a role allow-list and an optional WHERE clause — extending the same role/row scoping used on tables to bespoke endpoints.
erb_features.source_text: A per-endpoint access editor that sets RoleVisibility on each APIEndpoints row, so a contest action is available to representatives but a refund only to managers. An admin tunes who can fire which verb. Endpoint security is a row, edited in the UI.

erb_features.name: core-package-toggle
erb_features.title: Package enable/disable toggle
erb_features.description: A switch per package that flips its active flag so the entire UI responds — the package's routes, tables, and features disappear (or reappear) across the app at once, letting you demo the simpler product a non-admin sees.
erb_features.source_text: Enables or disables whole ERBPackages via an IsActive toggle, lighting up or dimming every feature, table, and route under that package at once. An admin turns the assistant package off for a tenant. The toggle cascades through the catalog.

erb_features.name: core-package-licensing
erb_features.title: Package licensing toggle
erb_features.description: A per-package licensed flag that fences an entire package behind the vendor licensing model, so every route, table, and feature it owns is hidden from accounts while remaining visible to Effortless staff.
erb_features.source_text: Controls per-package licensing with an IsLicensed flag on ERBPackages that the unlicensed-reveal surface reads to gate paid capabilities. An admin sells the rules-engine package as a tier. Licensing state is data the whole UI respects.

erb_features.name: core-feature-licensing
erb_features.title: Per-feature licensing toggle
erb_features.description: The LICENSED/UNLICENSED switch on each feature card and detail page, flipping a single feature's own licensing flag independently of its package — used to fence off individual vendor-tooling features.
erb_features.source_text: Controls per-feature licensing via ERBFeatures.IsLicensed so individual capabilities can be gated even within a licensed package. An admin offers the AI assistant as an add-on. Granular licensing is a per-row flag.

erb_features.name: core-table-route-licensing
erb_features.title: Per-table & per-route licensing toggles
erb_features.description: Licensing flags at the individual table and route level, so a single catalog table or navigation destination can be hidden from accounts without disabling its whole package — the finest grain of the licensing model.
erb_features.source_text: Adds per-table and per-route licensing toggles (IsLicensed on ERBTables and PlatformNaviation) so a tier can expose a screen while withholding the underlying editable table. An admin shows read-only jurisdictions to a lower tier. Every surface has its own license switch.

erb_features.name: core-table-catalog
erb_features.title: Self-describing table catalog
erb_features.description: A browsable card grid of every rulebook table — package-gated and clickable through to each table's permission/detail page. The schema describes itself, so the catalog is generated, never hand-listed.
erb_features.source_text: Renders the self-describing table catalog from ERBTables rows -- name, package, field count, catalog flag, per-role CRUD -- so the platform documents its own schema. A developer browses every table and its governance from one screen. The catalog is generated, never written by hand.

erb_features.name: core-fields-catalog
erb_features.title: Fields catalog
erb_features.description: A live grid of every field across all tables — name, datatype, type (raw/calculated/lookup/relationship), and description — giving a single searchable index of the entire data model's columns.
erb_features.source_text: Renders the fields catalog from ERBFields rows -- table, field, type, datatype, description -- the column-level companion to the table catalog. A developer inspects exactly how each calculated or lookup field is defined. It is the field-level self-description of the rulebook.

erb_features.name: core-explainer-dag
erb_features.title: Explainer DAG (calculated-field provenance)
erb_features.description: A full-screen, interactive inference graph for any calculated field: click a value and trace its derivation back through lookups, intermediate calcs, and raw inputs — the platform showing exactly how a number was produced.
erb_features.source_text: Builds the Explainer DAG that visualizes calculated-field provenance -- click any computed cell and trace raw inputs -> lookups -> calcs -> aggregations -- generated from the rulebook's formula graph. A user understands exactly how ResponseDeadline or ActivePoints was derived. It makes the inference graph witnessable.

erb_features.name: core-feature-catalog-grid
erb_features.title: Feature catalog grid (filterable cards)
erb_features.description: The Features page itself: a horizontal, filterable grid where every feature is a card with its own logo, searchable and narrowable by two orthogonal axes — lifecycle status and functional category. This very catalog is the feature.
erb_features.source_text: Presents the feature catalog as a filterable grid of cards from ERBFeatures, each with title, status, package, and cartoon logo. A product owner filters by status or package to see the platform's surface. This is the home of the very rows Loop 1 enriches.

erb_features.name: core-feature-detail-editor
erb_features.title: Feature detail editor
erb_features.description: The full-page dashboard for one feature — hero logo, stat strip, description, source narrative, rule refs, and metadata — with inline editing of title, description, status, category, sort order, rules, and sources.
erb_features.source_text: A feature detail editor for one ERBFeatures row -- title, description, SourceText, RuleRefs, status, route, image -- writing back to the rulebook. An admin documents a capability in place. The editor maintains the provenance spine this loop seeds.

erb_features.name: core-feature-vocab-editors
erb_features.title: Feature status & category editors
erb_features.description: Drag-reorderable editors for the two feature vocabularies — lifecycle statuses and functional categories — where each bucket's title, description, ordering, and flags are edited inline, including a per-status page that reorders the features within it.
erb_features.source_text: Provides editors for the feature vocabulary -- ERBFeatureStatuses and ERBFeatureCategories rows -- so the controlled lists behind the catalog are themselves editable data. An admin renames a status or adds a category. The taxonomy is rulebook-managed.

erb_features.name: core-feature-logo-system
erb_features.title: Cartoon feature-logo system
erb_features.description: The convention that gives every feature its own cartoon logo by id (/feature-logos/<id>.png), with a graceful category-emoji fallback when an image is missing, plus a script that crops and resizes generated art to the standard tile.
erb_features.source_text: Runs the cartoon feature-logo system that attaches a generated ImageUrl to each ERBFeatures row for the catalog grid. An admin regenerates a logo and the card updates. Imagery is a per-feature data attribute.

erb_features.name: core-glossary-admin
erb_features.title: Glossary admin
erb_features.description: A drag-reorderable, inline-editable glossary of platform terms organized into categories, so the shared vocabulary lives in the rulebook and stays consistent across the app and its docs.
erb_features.source_text: Gives admins glossary administration over GlossaryTerms and GlossaryCategories rows so the domain vocabulary stays current and complete. An admin adds 'collections' the moment a rule references it. The glossary is edited as first-class data.

erb_features.name: core-business-rule-admin
erb_features.title: Business-rule library admin
erb_features.description: A categorized, reorderable library of the platform's business rules (the R-codes features reference), edited inline and promoted to the rulebook — the human-readable companion to the formulas the engine enforces.
erb_features.source_text: Provides business-rule library administration over BusinessRules and BusinessRuleCategories rows -- the numbered TT-* rules that features cite via RuleRefs. An admin authors a rule and links its SchemaLocation. Loop 2 fills this library so every RuleRef resolves.

erb_features.name: core-site-branding
erb_features.title: Site-branding editor
erb_features.description: A single-row editor for the platform's identity — logo, colors, title, contact, and SEO — that applies the theme live as you type and serves public branding on the pre-auth login screen, then promotes to the rulebook on SAVE.
erb_features.source_text: A site-branding editor over the SiteBranding row -- company name, colors, logos, contact info, OG tags -- so the portal's identity is data. An admin rebrands the whole app from one screen. Branding is configuration, not CSS edits.

erb_features.name: core-global-ui-settings
erb_features.title: Global UI settings
erb_features.description: Browser-level workspace preferences exposed on the System Config page — such as toggling calculated-field provenance glyphs and compact table density — stored locally so each operator can tune their own view.
erb_features.source_text: Exposes global UI settings (theme, density, defaults) backed by branding and meta rows that the frontend reads at boot. An admin tunes the look and feel for every user. Settings are stored, not compiled.

erb_features.name: core-state-machine-admin
erb_features.title: State-machine admin (visual + edit)
erb_features.description: An admin surface for the generic state machines that drive entity lifecycles: a read-only flow diagram and transition log on one tab, and forms to edit machines, states, and transition rules on another.
erb_features.source_text: Offers visual state-machine administration -- view and edit StateMachines, MachineStates, and StateTransitionRules rows -- for the four traffic-ticket tracks. An admin adds a guarded transition as data. Loop 5 completes these machines.

erb_features.name: core-claim-lifecycle-sim
erb_features.title: Entity lifecycle simulator
erb_features.description: An operational tool that walks a record forward and backward through its lifecycle state machine, so an operator can advance, replay, or correct a record's stage and see the resulting transitions logged.
erb_features.source_text: Provides an entity lifecycle simulator that walks a sample citation through its state machine -- firing transitions, checking guards, logging StateTransitions -- to validate the model before real data. A developer dry-runs the citation lifecycle. It proves the machine is well-formed.

erb_features.name: as-portal-assistant
erb_features.title: Portal assistant (context-aware chat)
erb_features.description: A floating chat assistant that reads the current URL context (record, account, related entity) and runs a classify-then-answer flow grounded in that context, with an inspector that shows exactly what context it used.
erb_features.source_text: The context-aware portal assistant chats about the current screen, citation, or rule, logging each exchange as AssistantTurns rows with model and cost. A user asks the assistant about whatever they are looking at. It grounds answers in the live vw_* data and the rulebook.

erb_features.name: as-cost-dashboard
erb_features.title: Cost-management dashboard
erb_features.description: An analytics dashboard that rolls up assistant spend by model, account, record, and turn kind, backed by a versioned model price book — with drill-downs into per-account, per-record, and per-model detail.
erb_features.source_text: A cost-management dashboard aggregating AssistantTurns by model and day against ModelPricingVersions to show spend and token volume. A manager watches assistant cost trend over time. Every figure is a live aggregation of logged turns.

erb_features.name: as-cost-telemetry
erb_features.title: Per-turn cost telemetry
erb_features.description: Every assistant interaction is persisted as an AssistantTurns row with its token usage and computed cost, which then rolls up to the owning record and account — the data foundation the cost dashboard reads.
erb_features.source_text: Captures per-turn cost telemetry on each AssistantTurns row -- input tokens, output tokens, model, computed cost via ModelPricingVersions -- so spend is attributable to the turn. A developer audits a single expensive exchange. Cost is a stored, derived fact per turn.

erb_features.name: as-ocr-cost-estimator
erb_features.title: OCR cost estimator
erb_features.description: An interactive planning tool with draggable dividers and sliders for modeling OCR routing and token allocation, so the cost of extracting a document set can be estimated before the work is run.
erb_features.source_text: An OCR cost estimator that projects the token and dollar cost of processing a batch of citation images before running it, using AiModels and ModelPricingVersions rates. A manager budgets an intake batch up front. The estimate uses the same pricing rows that bill real turns.

erb_fields.name: Citations.CitationNumber
erb_fields.description: Human-readable citation number, e.g. TC-2026-0002.

erb_fields.name: Citations.Driver
erb_fields.description: FK to the cited driver.

erb_fields.name: Citations.ViolationType
erb_fields.description: FK to the violation type.

erb_fields.name: Citations.Jurisdiction
erb_fields.description: FK to the issuing jurisdiction (source of all deadlines/fines).

erb_fields.name: Citations.IssuedOn
erb_fields.description: Date the citation was issued.

erb_fields.name: Citations.ResponseDueDate
erb_fields.description: IssuedOn + Jurisdiction.DaysToRespond. Re-derived whenever the rule changes.

erb_fields.name: Citations.CitationStatus
erb_fields.description: Computed top-level status track; never stored.

erb_fields.name: Citations.ContestStatus
erb_fields.description: Computed contest track from the latest hearing.

erb_fields.name: Citations.PaymentStatus
erb_fields.description: Computed payment track including late penalty / collections.

erb_fields.name: Drivers.ActivePoints
erb_fields.description: Sum of points from the driver's adjudicated, non-dismissed citations.

erb_fields.name: Drivers.LicenseStatus
erb_fields.description: Valid → Warning → Suspended against the jurisdiction thresholds.

erb_fields.name: Hearings.Outcome
erb_fields.description: Pending | Dismissed | Upheld — drives downstream liability.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.Name
erb_fields.description: Logical key — lowercased rule code.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.RuleCode
erb_fields.description: Stable rule identifier (R1, R2, ... R38).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.Title
erb_fields.description: Short title of the rule.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.Category
erb_fields.description: FK to BusinessRuleCategories — the category bucket this rule belongs to (ROUTING | hard-stop | soft-flag | high-risk | SCORING | DECISION | REVIEW | SUBMISSION | data-integrity).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.SortOrder
erb_fields.description: Display order of the rule within its category (drag/drop sortable).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.Description
erb_fields.description: Full rule statement from the platform narrative.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.SchemaLocation
erb_fields.description: Where the rule is enforced in the schema (table.field or formula reference).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.CreatedAt
erb_fields.description: Audit: when this row was first inserted. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on INSERT); immutable thereafter.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.CreatedBy
erb_fields.description: Audit: the OWNER — the JWT user (auth.email()) who created this row. Auto-stamped on INSERT; immutable thereafter. NULL for build-time seed rows (no signed-in user).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.ModifiedAt
erb_fields.description: Audit: when this row was last written. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on every INSERT/UPDATE).

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.ModifiedBy
erb_fields.description: Audit: the JWT user (auth.email()) who last wrote this row. Auto-stamped on every INSERT/UPDATE.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRules.ModifiedByModel
erb_fields.description: Audit: the AI model credited on the last save when an LLM made/assisted the change (e.g. "gpt-4o"). NULL for plain human writes. Read from the app.modified_by_model session GUC by the audit trigger. The owner (CreatedBy/ModifiedBy) is always the human JWT user, never a model.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRuleCategories.BusinessRuleCategoryId
erb_fields.description: PK = slugified category key (routing / hard-stop / soft-flag / high-risk / scoring / decision / review / submission / data-integrity) — matches the slug form BusinessRules.Category links resolve to.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRuleCategories.Name
erb_fields.description: Echoes BusinessRuleCategoryId.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRuleCategories.Title
erb_fields.description: Human-readable category title shown on the category card.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRuleCategories.Description
erb_fields.description: What this category groups.

erb_fields.name: BusinessRuleCategories.SortOrder

glossary_terms.name: driver
glossary_terms.definition: The cited party — the person who received the traffic citation and whose license points roll up across their citations.

glossary_terms.name: representative
glossary_terms.definition: A line agent who owns cases and completes domain workflows on behalf of, or alongside, the driver.

glossary_terms.name: manager
glossary_terms.definition: A supervisor who schedules hearings and reviews/approves submissions.

glossary_terms.name: citation
glossary_terms.definition: A traffic ticket: one driver, one violation type, one issuing jurisdiction, an issue date, and the case hub from which all four status tracks are derived.

glossary_terms.name: jurisdiction
glossary_terms.definition: The regulatory authority (county or city) that issued a citation. Its row holds every deadline, fine, penalty, and point threshold that governs cases under it.

glossary_terms.name: hearing
glossary_terms.definition: A contest event: requested by the driver, scheduled by a manager, and concluded with an outcome (e.g. Dismissed) that drives liability.

glossary_terms.name: rules-engine
glossary_terms.definition: The pattern of expressing regulations as data on the Jurisdictions table, so changing a value re-derives every dependent citation with no code change.

glossary_terms.name: citation-status
glossary_terms.definition: The top-level computed track: Issued → Responded → InContest → Adjudicated → Closed.

glossary_terms.name: contest-status
glossary_terms.definition: The hearing track: NotContested | HearingRequested → Scheduled → Heard.

glossary_terms.name: payment-status
glossary_terms.definition: The money track: Pending → Due → Late → Collections | Paid | NotOwed.

glossary_terms.name: license-status
glossary_terms.definition: The driver track: Valid → Warning → Suspended, driven by active points against jurisdiction thresholds.

glossary_terms.name: default-judgment
glossary_terms.definition: What happens when a citation's response window passes with no response — it is adjudicated against the driver automatically.

glossary_terms.name: fine
glossary_terms.definition: The base monetary penalty for a violation, taken from the violation type's BaseFineUsd.

glossary_terms.name: late-penalty
glossary_terms.definition: An additional charge of LatePenaltyPct of the fine, applied when payment misses the pay-by date.

glossary_terms.name: collections
glossary_terms.definition: The terminal payment state reached when a citation remains unpaid beyond the jurisdiction's DaysLateToCollections window.

glossary_terms.name: points
glossary_terms.definition: Demerit points attached to a violation type; they accumulate on the driver and can trigger a license warning or suspension.

glossary_terms.name: adjudication
glossary_terms.definition: The recorded outcome of a contested citation after a hearing — upheld, reduced, or dismissed — which advances the citation-lifecycle to its adjudicated state.

glossary_terms.name: determination
glossary_terms.definition: The formal ruling on a contest, captured on the Citation and rendered into a determination letter from the jurisdiction template.

glossary_terms.name: contest-ground
glossary_terms.definition: A recognized legal basis for disputing a citation (signage, malfunction, emergency, calibration, mistaken identity), drawn from the ContestGrounds catalog per ViolationType.

glossary_terms.name: fee-schedule
glossary_terms.definition: The per-(jurisdiction, violation) base fine and surcharge percentage in FeeSchedules that drives a citation's amount due.

glossary_terms.name: deadline-rule
glossary_terms.definition: A per-jurisdiction window (contest, payment, appeal) in DeadlineRules that determines a citation's computed deadlines and late penalties.

glossary_terms.name: surcharge
glossary_terms.definition: A percentage added to the base fine per jurisdiction, contributing to the total amount due on a citation.

glossary_terms.name: work-queue
glossary_terms.definition: The prioritized list of non-terminal items (deadlines, hearings, payments) a role must act on, scoped by that role's WHERE policy.

glossary_terms.name: state-machine
glossary_terms.definition: A data-defined lifecycle (citation-lifecycle, contest-track, payment-track, license-track) of states and guarded transitions enforced by the backbone.

glossary_terms.name: transition-guard
glossary_terms.definition: The condition (referencing a business rule) that must hold for a state transition to fire, plus the role allowed to fire it.

glossary_terms.name: rbac
glossary_terms.definition: Role-Based Access Control: the role->table->field CRUD model plus WHERE policies and redaction that govern who can do what.

glossary_terms.name: row-level-security
glossary_terms.definition: Derived Postgres predicates that scope each role's visible rows (e.g. a representative sees only assigned citations), compiled from WHERE policies.

glossary_terms.name: redaction
glossary_terms.definition: Masking of PII fields (license number, address) for roles like external-llm at the moment a row leaves the database.

glossary_terms.name: licensing
glossary_terms.definition: Per-package/feature/table/route entitlement toggles that add or remove surfaces from the platform without code changes.

glossary_terms.name: explainer-dag
glossary_terms.definition: The visual inference graph showing how a calculated field (e.g. a contest deadline) is derived from raw inputs and lookups.

glossary_terms.name: portal-assistant
glossary_terms.definition: A context-aware chat that answers grounded in the current screen, role, and row, respecting permissions and redaction, with per-turn cost telemetry.

glossary_terms.name: cost-telemetry
glossary_terms.definition: Per-turn records of assistant/OCR token usage and dollar cost, rolled up by model, role, and case for the cost dashboard.

glossary_terms.name: business-rule
glossary_terms.definition: A numbered TT-* record stating a precise platform rule, linked from the features, transitions, and tests that implement and verify it.

glossary_terms.name: jurisdiction-rule
glossary_terms.definition: A per-state law governing fines, surcharges, deadlines, and point schedules, sourced from JurisdictionRules.

glossary_terms.name: driver-portal
glossary_terms.definition: The public self-service surface where a driver looks up their own citation and chooses to pay or contest.

glossary_terms.name: determination-letter
glossary_terms.definition: The official outcome document generated from a hearing determination using the jurisdiction's template.

jurisdiction_rules.name: ca-vc-§40519
jurisdiction_rules.title: 21-Day Response Window
jurisdiction_rules.description: An infraction defendant must appear or post bail within 21 days of the notice to appear; otherwise a civil assessment and collections referral may follow.
jurisdiction_rules.ai_version: In LA County you have 21 days from your ticket date to pay or ask for a hearing. Miss it and the court can decide against you and add a collection fee.

jurisdiction_rules.name: ca-la-ts-1
jurisdiction_rules.title: Traffic School Masks One Point
jurisdiction_rules.description: An eligible driver may attend traffic school once per 18 months to mask one point from a qualifying moving violation.
jurisdiction_rules.ai_version: In LA County you can take traffic school once every 18 months to hide one point from your record.

jurisdiction_rules.name: ny-vtl-§510
jurisdiction_rules.title: 11-Point Suspension Threshold
jurisdiction_rules.description: Accumulating 11 points within 18 months may result in license suspension; a warning is appropriate well before that.
jurisdiction_rules.ai_version: In NYC, 11 points in 18 months can get your license suspended — we flag a warning at 6.

jurisdiction_rules.name: tx-tc-§543
jurisdiction_rules.title: 14-Day Response Window
jurisdiction_rules.description: A defendant must respond to a citation within the period stated on the notice, commonly 14 days, or a warrant and additional fees may issue.
jurisdiction_rules.ai_version: In Travis County you usually have 14 days to respond to a ticket before a warrant and extra fees can be added.

jurisdiction_rules.name: tx-aus-ab-2025-114
jurisdiction_rules.title: No Calibration Records → Dismissal
jurisdiction_rules.description: If the agency cannot produce radar/lidar calibration records on timely request, the speed reading is unreliable and the citation must be dismissed.
jurisdiction_rules.ai_version: In Travis County, if the police can't show their radar was calibrated, a speeding ticket can be thrown out — exactly what happened on TC-2026-0003.

jurisdiction_source_documents.name: california-vehicle-code-—-arraignment-&-bail-deadlines
jurisdiction_source_documents.title: California Vehicle Code — Arraignment & Bail Deadlines
jurisdiction_source_documents.extracted_text: A defendant cited for an infraction must appear or pay bail within the time set by the court, generally within 21 days of the notice to appear. Failure to appear may result in a civil assessment and referral for collection.
jurisdiction_source_documents.notes: Source for CA-LA DaysToRespond = 21 and the default-judgment behavior.

jurisdiction_source_documents.name: los-angeles-county-traffic-school-eligibility-guidance
jurisdiction_source_documents.title: Los Angeles County Traffic School Eligibility Guidance
jurisdiction_source_documents.extracted_text: Eligible drivers may attend traffic school once every 18 months to mask one point from a qualifying moving violation. Commercial license holders and certain violations are excluded.

jurisdiction_source_documents.name: new-york-vehicle-&-traffic-law-—-point-system
jurisdiction_source_documents.title: New York Vehicle & Traffic Law — Point System
jurisdiction_source_documents.extracted_text: The NYS driver point system assigns points by violation. Accumulating 11 points within 18 months may result in license suspension; the DMV may also act on fewer points for serious offenses.
jurisdiction_source_documents.notes: Source for NY-NYC PointSuspensionThreshold = 11 and PointWarningThreshold = 6.

jurisdiction_source_documents.name: texas-transportation-code-—-speed-&-signal-offenses
jurisdiction_source_documents.title: Texas Transportation Code — Speed & Signal Offenses
jurisdiction_source_documents.extracted_text: An operator shall comply with posted speed limits and traffic-control signals. A defendant must respond to a citation within the period stated on the notice, commonly 14 days, or a warrant and additional fees may issue.
jurisdiction_source_documents.notes: Source for TX-AUS DaysToRespond = 14 and signal/speed violation definitions.

jurisdiction_source_documents.name: travis-county-appeal-board-decision-2025-114-(radar-calibration)
jurisdiction_source_documents.title: Travis County Appeal Board Decision 2025-114 (Radar Calibration)
jurisdiction_source_documents.extracted_text: Where the issuing agency cannot produce radar/lidar calibration records upon timely request, the speed measurement is unreliable and the citation must be dismissed. Calibration logs must be retained and produced at hearing.
jurisdiction_source_documents.notes: Directly supports the dismissal of citation TC-2026-0003 (Carlos Mendez) at hearing on 2026-04-15.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R1
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R1 — Citation requires driver, violation and jurisdiction
test_case.description: A citation must reference exactly one driver, one violation type, and one issuing jurisdiction.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R2
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R2 — Response due date is derived from the jurisdiction
test_case.description: ResponseDueDate = IssuedOn + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond. Changing the jurisdiction's rule re-derives every citation under it.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R3
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R3 — A response is pay or contest
test_case.description: Responding means either paying the fine or requesting a hearing; either sets RespondedOn and advances the citation to Responded.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R10
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R10 — Citation status is computed, never stored
test_case.description: CitationStatus is re-derived on every read from raw facts and child events; there is no stored status column to drift.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R11
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R11 — No response by deadline is a default judgment
test_case.description: If the response window passes with no RespondedOn, the citation moves to Adjudicated by default.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R12
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R12 — Contest status follows the latest hearing
test_case.description: ContestStatus is derived from the newest related hearing: NotContested | HearingRequested → Scheduled → Heard.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R13
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R13 — Only a manager schedules a hearing
test_case.description: Transitioning a hearing from HearingRequested to Scheduled is a manager-role action.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R20
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R20 — Fine is the violation's base fine
test_case.description: The amount owed starts at the violation type's BaseFineUsd for the citation's jurisdiction.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R21
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R21 — Late payment incurs a jurisdiction penalty
test_case.description: If payment is not made by the pay-by date, a penalty of LatePenaltyPct of the fine is added.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R22
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R22 — Prolonged non-payment goes to collections
test_case.description: A Late citation becomes Collections after DaysLateToCollections days past the pay-by date.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R23
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R23 — A dismissed citation owes nothing
test_case.description: If a hearing dismisses the citation, PaymentStatus is NotOwed regardless of the fine.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R30
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R30 — Active points roll up to the driver
test_case.description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from adjudicated, non-dismissed citations.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R31
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R31 — Points drive license warning then suspension
test_case.description: LicenseStatus is Warning at the jurisdiction's PointWarningThreshold and Suspended at PointSuspensionThreshold.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R40
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R40 — Regulations are data, not code
test_case.description: Every regulatory knob — deadlines, fines, penalties, thresholds, school caps — is a column on Jurisdictions, editable without code changes.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R50
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R50 — Overdue work is urgent
test_case.description: A work-queue item whose due date is in the past is urgent and sorts to the top.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R51
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R51 — Work items mirror their subject's deadline
test_case.description: A work item's DueDate is carried from its subject (e.g. Citations.ResponseDueDate or PaymentDueDate).

test_case.name: tc-rule-R60
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R60 — Overrides require a reason
test_case.description: Any OVERRIDE audit entry must carry a non-empty Reason; the trail is append-only.

test_case.name: tc-rule-R70
test_case.title: Rule enforced: R70 — Every assistant turn is costed
test_case.description: Each assistant turn records input/output tokens and the exact pricing version used, so TotalCost is fully derivable.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-INTAKE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-INTAKE-01 — Citation requires driver, violation, jurisdiction
test_case.description: A citation must reference exactly one Driver, one ViolationType, and one issuing Jurisdiction; none may be null at intake.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-INTAKE-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-INTAKE-02 — Issue date present and not future-dated
test_case.description: Every citation records an IssueDate that is on or before today; a future issue date is rejected at intake.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-INTAKE-03
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-INTAKE-03 — Driver response is pay-or-contest before the deadline
test_case.description: The driver's response is one of {pay, contest} and must be recorded on or before the computed ResponseDeadline.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-DEADLINE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-DEADLINE-01 — Response deadline derives from jurisdiction DaysToRespond
test_case.description: ResponseDeadline = IssueDate + the issuing jurisdiction's DaysToRespond; it recomputes whenever the rule changes.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-CITATION-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-CITATION-01 — Citation status is derived, never stored
test_case.description: CitationStatus (Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed) is computed on read from facts and child CaseEvents; no stored status column is authoritative.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-CITATION-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-CITATION-02 — Status order is monotonic
test_case.description: A citation may only advance forward through its lifecycle states; backward transitions require an explicit, logged override.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-CONTEST-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-CONTEST-01 — Contesting requires a timely contest response
test_case.description: The contest track only opens when DriverResponse = contest was recorded before the ResponseDeadline.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-CONTEST-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-CONTEST-02 — Contest track derives from the latest hearing
test_case.description: ContestStatus (NotContested | HearingRequested -> Scheduled -> Heard) is derived from the most recent Hearings row for the citation.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-CONTEST-03
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-CONTEST-03 — Determination decides liability
test_case.description: A hearing outcome of dismissed sets liability to none and zero fine owed; upheld confirms the original fine and points.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-HEARING-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-HEARING-01 — Hearing requires a requested contest
test_case.description: A Hearings row may only be created for a citation whose ContestStatus is HearingRequested or later.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-HEARING-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-HEARING-02 — Scheduling is manager-or-admin only
test_case.description: Only manager or admin roles may set a hearing's ScheduledDate; representatives request, they do not schedule.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PAYMENT-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PAYMENT-01 — Payment track derives from payments and pay-by date
test_case.description: PaymentStatus (Pending -> Due -> Late -> Collections | Paid | NotOwed) is computed from Payments rows and the jurisdiction pay-by date.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PAYMENT-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PAYMENT-02 — Late penalty applies after the pay-by date
test_case.description: Once the pay-by date passes with no full payment, the jurisdiction's LatePenaltyPercent is added to AmountOwed.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PAYMENT-03
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PAYMENT-03 — Paid in full closes the case
test_case.description: When recorded Payments equal AmountOwed, PaymentStatus becomes Paid and the citation advances toward Closed.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-FEE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-FEE-01 — Base fine comes from the violation and jurisdiction
test_case.description: The base fine is the ViolationType base amount adjusted by the jurisdiction's fee schedule; it is data, not a constant.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-LICENSE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-LICENSE-01 — Active points roll up across a driver's citations
test_case.description: A driver's ActivePoints is the sum of points from non-dismissed, non-expired citations under each jurisdiction's point window.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-LICENSE-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-LICENSE-02 — License track follows jurisdiction thresholds
test_case.description: LicenseStatus (Valid -> Warning -> Suspended) is derived by comparing ActivePoints against the jurisdiction's warning and suspension thresholds.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-QUEUE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-QUEUE-01 — Work queue is computed from deadlines and status
test_case.description: WorkQueueItems are derived from overdue responses, due/late payments, and upcoming hearings, bucketed by urgency; nothing is hand-enqueued.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-AUDIT-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-AUDIT-01 — Every state-affecting change is logged
test_case.description: Each status change, override, payment, and edit writes an append-only AuditLogEntries (and where lifecycle-relevant, a CaseEvents) row.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-AUDIT-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-AUDIT-02 — The log never contradicts the derived state
test_case.description: The append-only history explains how current computed state was reached; it is additive narration, never an alternate source of truth.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-ASSISTANT-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-ASSISTANT-01 — Assistant answers are grounded in live data
test_case.description: The assistant answers about a citation/rule/portal from live vw_* reads and the rulebook, recording each exchange as an AssistantTurns row.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-ASSISTANT-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-ASSISTANT-02 — Every turn is cost-accounted
test_case.description: Each AssistantTurns row records input/output tokens and a computed cost via ModelPricingVersions for the turn's AiModel.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RULES-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RULES-01 — Jurisdiction knobs are editable data
test_case.description: Deadlines, fines, penalty percentages, and point thresholds live in Jurisdictions/JurisdictionRules and every dependent value re-derives on edit.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RULES-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RULES-02 — Each jurisdiction rule cites its source
test_case.description: A JurisdictionRules row links to the JurisdictionSourceDocuments / ReferenceDocuments authority that justifies it.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RBAC-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RBAC-01 — Four canonical roles govern access
test_case.description: Exactly four roles exist (admin, manager, representative, external-llm) and every permission decision references one of them.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RBAC-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RBAC-02 — CRUD is per role, per table, per field
test_case.description: What each role may create/read/update/delete is data at the table and field grain; the enforced API consults it on every operation.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RBAC-03
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RBAC-03 — Row access follows per-role WHERE policies
test_case.description: Each role-table pair carries a WHERE policy; a representative sees only their own citations while admin sees all, enforced on every vw_* read.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-RBAC-04
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-RBAC-04 — Lower-trust roles get redacted projections
test_case.description: Fields denied to a role (e.g. PII for external-llm) are stripped from responses at projection time, not nulled afterward.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-NAV-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-NAV-01 — Navigation is derived from PlatformNaviation rows
test_case.description: The sidebar and route tree render from PlatformNaviation filtered by the current role's RoleVisibility; there is no hand-maintained menu.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-NAV-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-NAV-02 — Route order and pinning are data
test_case.description: NavLevel, SortOrder, and PinToTop on PlatformNaviation determine ordering and which screens float to the top.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-AUTH-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-AUTH-01 — Identity is resolved per request from the magic-link session
test_case.description: Each request resolves to an AppUsers row and role via the MagicLinkConfig flow; identity feeds every RBAC and scoping decision.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-LICENSE-PKG-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-LICENSE-PKG-01 — Surfaces are gated by license/active flags
test_case.description: Packages, features, tables, and routes carry IsLicensed/IsActive flags; unlicensed surfaces are revealed as upgrade prompts, not deleted.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PLATFORM-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PLATFORM-01 — The rulebook JSON is the single source of truth
test_case.description: All substrates (Postgres, Python, explain-dag, rulespeak) are mechanically derived from the rulebook by effortless build; edits go to the rulebook.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PLATFORM-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PLATFORM-02 — The platform describes itself
test_case.description: ERBTables/ERBFields/ERBFeatures/ERBPackages catalog every table, field, capability, and package so the app can render its own model.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-PLATFORM-03
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-PLATFORM-03 — Build is generate + load; drift is guarded
test_case.description: effortless build regenerates DDL/views/inserts and reloads the DB; a drift guard warns before a rebuild would clobber un-saved DB edits.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-GLOSSARY-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-GLOSSARY-01 — Domain terms are defined as data
test_case.description: Every domain term used in a feature or rule is defined in GlossaryTerms under a GlossaryCategories group.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-DETERMINATION-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-DETERMINATION-01 — Determination is recorded
test_case.description: A hearing determination (upheld / dismissed / reduced) must be recorded on the Citation before the citation-lifecycle may advance to adjudicated, and it writes a CaseEvents entry.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-DETERMINATION-02
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-DETERMINATION-02 — Dismissal reverses consequences
test_case.description: When a determination dismisses a Citation, any assessed license points are reversed and any paid amount is refunded, restoring the Driver to make-whole state.

test_case.name: tc-rule-TT-STATE-01
test_case.title: Rule enforced: TT-STATE-01 — Lifecycle transitions are guarded
test_case.description: Every state transition is gated by its guard condition and the firing role; the state-machine backbone rejects illegal transitions and logs each accepted one to CaseEvents.
